# Arduino-Embedded-Systems
# RC Cars

Two Arduino-based car projects exploring manual and autonomous control: a serial-commanded remote control car and an ultrasonic-sensor-driven self-driving car.

## 📁 Projects

| Project | Control Method | Key Component |
|---|---|---|
| [Remote Control Car](#-remote-control-car) | Serial commands (F/B/L/R/S) | Dual DC motors (L298N-style driver) |
| [Self-Driving Car](#-self-driving-car-obstacle-avoidance) | Autonomous obstacle avoidance | Ultrasonic sensor (HC-SR04) + servo |

---

## 🕹️ Remote Control Car

A two-motor car driven by single-character serial commands, using a standard H-bridge motor driver.

**File:** `remote control car/Remote control car code .ino`

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Remote control car chassis, top-down view" width="400"/>

### Pin Mapping

| Function | Pin |
|---|---|
| Left Motor Forward | 4 |
| Left Motor Backward | 5 |
| Right Motor Forward | 2 |
| Right Motor Backward | 3 |
| Left Motor Enable (PWM) | 9 |
| Right Motor Enable (PWM) | 10 |

### Commands (via Serial, 9600 baud)

| Character | Action |
|---|---|
| `F` | Move forward |
| `B` | Move backward |
| `R` | Turn right |
| `L` | Turn left |
| `S` | Stop |

Commands can be sent from the Arduino Serial Monitor, a Bluetooth module (e.g., HC-05), or any serial-capable controller (app, Python script, etc.) wired to the Arduino's RX/TX.

### How It Works

The loop continuously checks for incoming serial data. On receiving a character, it sets the corresponding motor pins HIGH/LOW to drive the wheels, with motor speed fixed via PWM on the enable pins (`analogWrite(..., 255)` — full speed).

## 🚗 Self-Driving Car (Obstacle Avoidance)

An autonomous car that drives forward and reroutes itself when it detects an obstacle, using an ultrasonic sensor mounted on a servo to "look" left and right.

**File:** `Self _ Driving Car using ultrasonic Sensor/Self_Driving Car Arduino code.ino`

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Self-driving car with ultrasonic sensor and servo mounted" width="400"/>

### Pin Mapping

| Function | Pin |
|---|---|
| Left Motor Forward | A5 |
| Left Motor Backward | A4 |
| Left Motor Enable (PWM) | 5 |
| Right Motor Forward | A3 |
| Right Motor Backward | A2 |
| Right Motor Enable (PWM) | 6 |
| Servo (sensor sweep) | 10 |
| Buzzer | 3 |
| Ultrasonic Trigger | 11 |
| Ultrasonic Echo | 12 |

### How It Works

1. The car drives forward while the ultrasonic sensor (centered via servo) continuously measures distance to the nearest obstacle.
2. If an obstacle is detected within **20 cm**:
   - The car stops and sounds the buzzer.
   - The servo sweeps to the left and right to measure available clearance on each side.
   - The car turns toward whichever side has more open space (by briefly pulsing the opposite-side motor).
3. If the path is clear, the car continues forward.

### Components Used

- Arduino Uno (or compatible)
- HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor
- SG90 (or similar) servo motor
- L298N motor driver (or equivalent H-bridge)
- 2× DC gear motors + wheels
- Buzzer
- Chassis + battery pack

---

## 🛠️ Getting Started

1. Open the desired `.ino` file in the [Arduino IDE](https://www.arduino.cc/en/software).
2. Wire the components according to the pin mapping tables above.
3. Select your board and port, then upload.
4. For the Remote Control Car, open the Serial Monitor (9600 baud) or connect a Bluetooth/serial controller to send `F`/`B`/`L`/`R`/`S` commands.
